facts.raw_span: A 66-year-old man presented with a 24-hour history of incomplete closure of the right eye
flattening of the right nasolabial fold
right-sided hemiplegia rendering him unable to sit up or stand
The patient had a 3-year history of hypertension
no history of neurological disorders
The patient was alert and oriented
Effacement of the right frontal wrinkle
Incomplete closure of the right eyelid
Muscle strength in the right upper and lower extremities: grade 0/5
Hypoesthesia noted on the right side
Right Babinski sign: positive
Hemorrhage in the left thalamus-radiation crown region and in the lateral ventricle at 24 hours postonset

rationales.F01: Incomplete closure of the right eye suggests a cranial nerve VII palsy, which can be seen in intracerebral hemorrhage.
rationales.F03: Right-sided hemiplegia is a strong indicator of a stroke syndrome, which can be caused by intracerebral hemorrhage or ischemic stroke.
rationales.F09: Muscle strength grade 0/5 in the right upper and lower extremities indicates a severe motor deficit, consistent with an upper motor neuron lesion.
rationales.F11: A positive Babinski sign is a strong indicator of an upper motor neuron lesion, which can be seen in intracerebral hemorrhage or ischemic stroke.
rationales.F12: Hemorrhage in the left thalamus-radiation crown region is diagnostic of intracerebral hemorrhage and rules out ischemic stroke.
